scope: Proposition B.5 (Two conditional Taylor budgets) of the manuscript “A sharp Fourier certificate for planar circle packing” (preprints/A-sharp-Fourier-certificate-for-planar-circle-packing-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 090 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3a532659c4aa989d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following choices give sufficient rational error enclosures for the same finite quantities used in Appendix A. For a basis input at n ∈ J = {1, 3, 4}, a row m ∈ J, y = 1, and ℓ = 0, 1, take D = 63, hD = 32, M = 106, and δ = 10−14 in (B.26). There are no atoms. If Qm, Dm have rational errors at most 10−25, either entry of (A.11) has error less than 2.13 · 10−13 < 10−12. For the full rational finite-input domain at the start of this subsection, take D = 255, hD = 128, M = 1053, and δ = 4 · 10−15 in (B.26), and require each of the seven atom-product radii in (B.25) to be at most 4 · 10−15/7. Each U and X moment then has error less than 10−14. For node rows m ∈ If , with rational Qm, Dm errors at most 10−25, either entry of (A.11) has error less than 1.8 · 10−14.
